q: The support system is very important to all living things such as plants, animals and ____ .
e: The support system is very important to all living things such as plants, animals and humans. Humans is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Plants do not have skeletons like animals but they use their ____ of cells within packing tissue for support.
e: Plants do not have skeletons like animals but they use their turgidity of cells within packing tissue for support. Turgidity is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In humans and other animals, the main body support is provided by the internal skeletal system of ____ .
e: In humans and other animals, the main body support is provided by the internal skeletal system of bones. Bones is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In some animals, the skeleton is ____ as in insects and prawns.
e: In some animals, the skeleton is external as in insects and prawns. External is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The skeleton supports body weight, maintains body shape, protects ____ organs inside the body.
e: The skeleton supports body weight, maintains body shape, protects soft organs inside the body. Soft is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Support in woody plants has specialized tissue to give them support, which has ____ cell wall.
e: Support in woody plants has specialized tissue to give them support, which has cellulose cell wall. Plant cell walls are made of cellulose.

q: The physiological support is a temporary support because it depends on the presence of ____ in the plant cells.
e: The physiological support is a temporary support because it depends on the presence of water in the plant cells. Water is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The structural support is a ____ support.
e: The structural support is a permanent support. Permanent is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Support in non-woody plants depends on the turgidity of their cells such as ____ and collenchyma.
e: Support in non-woody plants depends on the turgidity of their cells such as parenchyma and collenchyma. Parenchyma is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Roots which grow down from the stem or branches into the ground for support are called ____ roots.
e: Roots which grow down from the stem or branches into the ground for support are called prop roots. Prop is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The thick support roots that grow from the stem above the ground are called ____ roots.
e: The thick support roots that grow from the stem above the ground are called buttress roots. Buttress is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The movement of a plant in response to light is known as ____ .
e: The movement of a plant in response to light is known as phototropism. Phototropism is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The movement of a plant part towards the soil in response to earth's gravity is known as ____ .
e: The movement of a plant part towards the soil in response to earth's gravity is known as geotropism. Geotropism is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The movement of the plant towards the water is known as ____ .
e: The movement of the plant towards the water is known as hydrotropism. Hydrotropism is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The movement of plants in response to a chemical stimulus is known as ____ .
e: The movement of plants in response to a chemical stimulus is known as chemotropism. Chemotropism is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The directional movement in plants in response to touch is known as ____ .
e: The directional movement in plants in response to touch is known as thigmotropism. Thigmotropism is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The movement of plant or their parts in response to changes in the external stimulus of temperature is known as ____ .
e: The movement of plant or their parts in response to changes in the external stimulus of temperature is known as thermotropism. Thermotropism is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Nastic movements in plants are not ____ movements.
e: Nastic movements in plants are not directional movements. Directional is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The leaves of ‘touch me not’ fold up immediately when ____ .
e: The leaves of ‘touch me not’ fold up immediately when touched. Touched is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The closing of the lid of insectivorous plant occurs due to the catchment of ____ .
e: The closing of the lid of insectivorous plant occurs due to the catchment of insects. Insects is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The skeletal system in animals is commonly recognized as hydrostatic skeleton, exoskeleton and ____ .
e: The skeletal system in animals is commonly recognized as hydrostatic skeleton, exoskeleton and endoskeleton. Endoskeleton is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Hydrostatic skeletons are found primarily in soft-bodied terrestrial invertebrates such as ____ .
e: Hydrostatic skeletons are found primarily in soft-bodied terrestrial invertebrates such as earthworms. Earthworms is the idea that completes this fact.

q: An exoskeleton is a rigid, hard case that surrounds the body of ____ .
e: An exoskeleton is a rigid, hard case that surrounds the body of arthropods. Arthropods is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Endoskeletons found in vertebrates are rigid internal ____ .
e: Endoskeletons found in vertebrates are rigid internal skeletons. The skeleton supports the body, protects organs, and gives muscles something to pull on.

q: The human skeleton has about ____ bones.
e: The human skeleton has about 206 bones. 206 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The bones of the skeleton provide sites for ____ attachment.
e: The bones of the skeleton provide sites for muscle attachment. The skeleton supports the body, protects organs, and gives muscles something to pull on.

q: The axial skeleton includes the bones found in the ____ and head of the body.
e: The axial skeleton includes the bones found in the trunk and head of the body. Trunk is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The axial skeleton includes the ____ pairs of ribs.
e: The axial skeleton includes the 12 pairs of ribs. Carbon-12 is the mass standard: one-twelfth of that atom is the atomic mass unit.

q: The appendicular skeleton is adapted to allow the body to ____ .
e: The appendicular skeleton is adapted to allow the body to move. Move is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The appendicular skeleton includes the bones in the limbs that extend from the ____ of the body.
e: The appendicular skeleton includes the bones in the limbs that extend from the trunk of the body. Trunk is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Bone tissue consists of a dense and hard organic matrix deposits of ____ in between the bone cells.
e: Bone tissue consists of a dense and hard organic matrix deposits of minerals in between the bone cells. Minerals is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Cartilage is a flexible connective tissue found between the ____ .
e: Cartilage is a flexible connective tissue found between the bones. Bones is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A joint is the place where two ____ meet.
e: A joint is the place where two bones meet. Bones is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Fibrous joints are made of the same dense material that bone is made of and they act like a tough ____ that connects the bones.
e: Fibrous joints are made of the same dense material that bone is made of and they act like a tough glue that connects the bones. Glue is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Cartilaginous joints allow ____ movement.
e: Cartilaginous joints allow partial movement. Partial is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Synovial joints are cushioned with cartilage and held together by a capsule of ____ .
e: Synovial joints are cushioned with cartilage and held together by a capsule of ligaments. Ligaments is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Synovial joints allow a great degree of ____ between bones.
e: Synovial joints allow a great degree of movement between bones. Movement is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The healthy musculoskeletal system allows for normal physical activities such as walking, running, ____ and other activities.
e: The healthy musculoskeletal system allows for normal physical activities such as walking, running, jumping and other activities. Jumping is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Abnormal joints and muscles result in ____ in which damaged ends of bones rub against each other.
e: Abnormal joints and muscles result in osteoarthritis in which damaged ends of bones rub against each other. Osteoarthritis is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Physical activities and exercises are necessary to maintain healthy ____ between bones.
e: Physical activities and exercises are necessary to maintain healthy joints between bones. Joints is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Some movements can cause injuries, leading to joint damage involving ____ and ligaments.
e: Some movements can cause injuries, leading to joint damage involving cartilages and ligaments. Cartilages is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Health of bones, joints and muscles can be supported by healthy ____ .
e: Health of bones, joints and muscles can be supported by healthy food. Food is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Vitamins C, K and A, iron, calcium, phosphorus and magnesium are good for ____ .
e: Vitamins C, K and A, iron, calcium, phosphorus and magnesium are good for joints. Joints is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Proteins play a critical role in muscle and cartilage ____ .
e: Proteins play a critical role in muscle and cartilage repair. Repair is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Reducing body weight by exercising regularly reduces joint pain, improves joint health and keeps ____ strong.
e: Reducing body weight by exercising regularly reduces joint pain, improves joint health and keeps muscle strong. Muscle is the idea that completes this fact.
